FR.name: 2027 budget bills (PLF and PLFSS 2027)
FR.what: The 2027 finance and social-security bills presented on 1 October 2026: about 54 billion euros of consolidation, of which 43 billion of new measures (including a freeze of the civil-service pay index and of basic pensions except the lowest).

claim.text: The public deficit falls from 5.4% of GDP in 2026 to 5.0% in 2027, with growth of 1.0% in 2027 after 0.5% and inflation of 1.8%.

source.label: Government forecasts, as set out in the HCFP opinion

assessment.text: The 1.0% growth assumption looks optimistic; most forecasters are one to three tenths lower and downside risks dominate. The spending path is achievable only if every measure is adopted, which depends on Parliament passing the bills.

deficit.text: Government target 5.0% of GDP in 2027 from 5.4%; HCFP: achievable only if all measures pass.

inflation.text: 1.8% in 2027, described by HCFP as consensual but exposed to energy prices.

growth.text: Government 1.0%; Banque de France 0.9%, OFCE 0.7% (Euronews, 1 Oct 2026).

consensus.note: Consensus = median of the IMF, OECD and Commission forecasts.
consensus.label: General government balance, % of GDP

view.question: Will France's 2027 budget law be promulgated by 31 December 2026?
view.point_label: My 2027 general government balance, % of GDP

FR.name: Pension reform suspension and the 2027 pension freeze
FR.what: The 2026 social-security financing law suspended the 2023 pension reform until 1 January 2028, freezing the legal age at 62 years and 9 months and the contribution period at 170 quarters. The 2027 bill proposes freezing basic pensions in 2027 except the lowest.

claim.text: The suspension is a pause, not a repeal: the 2023 rules resume after 1 January 2028, and the 2027 freeze is part of the bill's savings.

source.label: CMS Francis Lefebvre, on the LFSS 2026

assessment.text: Even after the under-indexation, pension benefits are one of the biggest spending increases in 2027 (+9 billion euros on the social-security field alone), behind interest costs.

deficit.text: Pension spending +9 billion euros in 2027 after the freeze (HCFP).

inflation.text: Not quantified in the cited sources.

growth.text: Not quantified in the cited sources.

FR.status: Suspension in force until 1 January 2028; the 2027 freeze is in the PLFSS 2027 before Parliament.

view.question: Will the 2027 freeze of basic pensions (except the lowest) be in the adopted LFSS 2027?

BR.name: Fiscal framework (LC 200/2023) and the 2027 primary target
BR.what: Since 2023 federal policy runs on an annual primary-balance target with a tolerance band of 0.25 point of GDP either side, plus a cap on real primary-spending growth. For 2027 the target is a central-government surplus of 0.5% of GDP.

claim.text: The 2027 budget bill puts the result counted for the target at a surplus of R$83.4 billion (0.6% of GDP) after legal deductions, above the R$73.2 billion (0.5% of GDP) target, so the government says the framework is being met.

source.label: Ministério do Planejamento, PLOA 2027 (as tabulated by IFI, RAF 116)

assessment.text: Formal compliance remains possible but rests on assumptions more optimistic than IFI's and a much thinner safety margin. In IFI's scenario the result counted for the target is a surplus of only R$0.9 billion, below even the lower tolerance bound, so about R$35.7 billion of discretionary spending would have to be frozen.

source.label: IFI, Relatório de Acompanhamento Fiscal nº 116

deficit.text: IFI projects a 2027 central-government primary deficit of R$86.1 billion (0.6% of GDP) before deductions, against the bill's R$18.6 billion surplus.

inflation.text: Not quantified for the framework itself in the cited sources.

growth.text: Not quantified for the framework itself in the cited sources.

BR.status: In force; the 2027 target is set in the budget guidelines bill (PLDO 2027).

consensus.note: Focus measures the consolidated public sector; the target is for the central government.
consensus.label: Primary balance, % of GDP

view.question: Will Brazil's central government meet its 2027 primary target (at least the 0.25% of GDP lower bound) without changing the target?
view.point_label: My 2027 primary balance, consolidated public sector, % of GDP

BR.name: 2027 budget bill (PLOA 2027)
BR.what: The 2027 annual budget bill (PLN 24/2026), sent to Congress on 31 August 2026. Congress's joint budget committee amends it and both chambers vote it in December.

claim.text: An effective central-government primary surplus of R$18.6 billion (0.1% of GDP) in 2027, built on 2.5% GDP growth and 3.6% IPCA inflation.

assessment.text: Revenue could fall short if growth is below the 2.5% assumed, and assumed savings from benefit reviews may not materialise. IFI expects pension spending of R$1,239.2 billion against the bill's R$1,215.1 billion, part of a R$104.8 billion gap between the two projections of the effective result.

source.label: IFI, Relatório de Acompanhamento Fiscal nº 116

deficit.text: Bill: surplus of R$18.6 billion; IFI: deficit of R$86.1 billion (0.6% of GDP).

inflation.text: IPCA 2027: bill 3.6%, IFI 4.0%, Focus median 4.3% (at the time of RAF 116).

growth.text: GDP 2027: bill 2.5%, IFI 1.8%, Focus median 1.5% (at the time of RAF 116).

consensus.note: The bill's revenue rests on its growth assumption.
consensus.label: Real GDP growth

view.question: Will Brazil's 2027 real GDP growth (first IBGE estimate) be at least the 2.5% the budget bill assumes?

BR.name: Consumption-tax reform (CBS and IBS)
BR.what: Constitutional Amendment 132/2023 and Complementary Law 214/2025 replace federal and local consumption taxes with a dual VAT. The federal CBS replaces PIS and Cofins from 1 January 2027; the state and municipal IBS is phased in afterwards. The reference CBS rate is still to be set.

claim.text: The government projects R$636 billion of CBS revenue in 2027 in the budget bill; the law includes a mechanism to cut rates if the combined burden of the new taxes rises.

assessment.text: The 2027 bill adds a R$33.8 billion payment into the fund that compensates states for replacing IPI with the selective tax. It sits outside the LC 200 spending cap but counts towards the primary target, an example of how the transition's design adds fiscal pressure.

source.label: IFI, Relatório de Acompanhamento Fiscal nº 116

deficit.text: R$33.8 billion compensation-fund payment in 2027, counted in the primary result (IFI).

inflation.text: Not quantified in the cited sources.

growth.text: Not quantified in the cited sources.

BR.status: CBS starts on 1 January 2027; the Senate must set the reference rate by 15 December 2026.

next.label: Senate deadline to set the CBS reference rate
next.title: Senate deadline to set the CBS reference rate

view.question: Will the Senate set the CBS reference rate by 15 December 2026?

MX.name: 2027 budget package (Paquete Económico 2027)
MX.what: The 2027 economic package (general policy criteria, revenue law and spending budget) presented to the Chamber of Deputies on 8 September 2026.

claim.text: The broadest deficit measure (RFSP) falls from 4.1% of GDP in 2026 to 3.9% in 2027, with a primary surplus and debt (SHRFSP) at 55% of GDP; growth of 1.5% to 2.5% and inflation of 3.0% in 2027.

source.label: SHCP, Criterios Generales de Política Económica 2027 (as summarised by IMCO)

assessment.text: The package lowers the ambition of fiscal consolidation (3.9% against the 3.5% planned in April) and cuts the growth outlook. Private analysts surveyed by Banxico expect 1.8% growth; if growth undershoots, revenue would miss and push the deficit and debt up.

MX.name: Judicial reform and the second judicial election
MX.what: The 2024 constitutional reform makes federal judges elected by popular vote; the first judicial election was held in June 2025. In May 2026 Congress approved moving the second judicial election from 2027 to June 2028.

claim.text: The government proposed the postponement so the judicial vote would not coincide with the June 2027 federal and state elections, citing the operational risks flagged by the electoral institute.

assessment.text: The reform creates important uncertainties about the effectiveness of contract enforcement and the predictability of the rule of law (2024 Article IV mission; not updated in the cited sources).

source.label: IMF, Mexico: 2024 Article IV mission concluding statement

MX.name: Energy policy and support for Pemex
MX.what: The 2025 energy laws give state firms Pemex and CFE priority. The Pemex Strategic Plan 2025-2035 (August 2025) and a Treasury capitalisation strategy aim to put Pemex's finances on a sustainable footing.

claim.text: The plan aims to make Pemex financially self-sufficient from 2027, no longer needing Treasury support.

source.label: Enerdata, on the Pemex Strategic Plan

assessment.text: The 2027 package still includes capital contributions to Pemex of 81.1 billion pesos (69.2% less than before), so the plan's original goal was not met. With losses of 28 billion pesos in the first half of 2026 and debt above US$77 billion, Pemex remains a risk to public finances.

items.name: IFI (Instituição Fiscal Independente, Federal Senate)
items.note: Report pages on www12.senado.leg.br sit behind a browser security check; the PDFs in the Senate digital library (www2.senado.leg.br) are open.
items.title: Relatório de Acompanhamento Fiscal – Out/2026
items.summary: The IFI expects a primary deficit of 0.5% of GDP in 2026 and a potential deficit of 1.0% of GDP in 2027, arguing that new spending commitments and lost revenue (about R$ 40 billion unbudgeted) call for a fiscal adjustment of roughly 3 percentage points of GDP. It also warns that the primary-result target misses large off-budget credit and fund operations, and that a higher neutral interest rate would raise the required primary surplus.

key_number.what: Potential primary deficit for 2027 as a percentage of GDP, which the IFI says could arise given new commitments and its differences from the PLOA 2027 figures

items.name: HCFP (Haut Conseil des finances publiques)
items.title: Avis n°2026 – 5 Lois de finances 2027
items.summary: The High Council of Public Finances judges the government's 2026 deficit forecast of 5.4% of GDP plausible, but considers the 2027 growth forecast of 1.0% optimistic and says risks to growth are mainly downward. It warns that the expected 2027 deficit reduction is too slow, that the debt-to-GDP ratio keeps rising toward about 122%, and that the 2029 target of a deficit below 3% of GDP is very unlikely to be met.

key_number.what: Expected public debt-to-GDP ratio, which the High Council says is approaching this level as debt keeps rising

items.name: Cour des comptes
items.note: Annual report on the situation and outlook of the public finances (published 25 June 2026).

items.name: México Evalúa
items.title: El reto del Paquete Económico 2027: recuperar el margen para invertir en desarrollo
items.summary: México Evalúa finds that the 2027 Economic Package would lower the broad public deficit (RFSP) to 3.9% of GDP, a real improvement, but still above the 2.5% the IMF recommends, and that this effort is not enough to stabilize debt. The think tank warns that meeting the targets depends on record tax collection, a sharp cut in support for Pemex, and tight spending, with any shortfall likely falling on investment, health and education.

key_number.what: Projected broad public deficit (RFSP) as a share of GDP in 2027 if the Economic Package is approved, 1.9 points below 2024

items.name: IMEF (Instituto Mexicano de Ejecutivos de Finanzas)
items.title: Información estratégica para líderes financieros: nuevo reporte IMEF
items.summary: The IMEF says Mexico's public finances are under pressure, with a broad public-sector deficit of 4.8% at the end of 2025, well above the 3.9% the government initially planned. It warns that high debt, continued support for Pemex and new labour costs bring Mexico closer to losing its investment-grade rating, and it expects weak growth of 1.3% in 2026.

key_number.what: The broad public-sector fiscal deficit (RFSP) at the close of 2025, well above the 3.9% initially planned by the government.
